statement: Perceived automation can reduce evaluation apprehension and support disclosure, but this advantage is conditional on trust and does not establish truthful reporting.
scope: Short virtual-human and automated health or survey interactions; evidence does not establish accuracy of sensitive disclosures.

evidence.rationale: Randomized machine framing reduced disclosure fear and impression management.
Behavioral and blind-observer measures converged with self-report under machine framing.
Automatic and Wizard-of-Oz cohorts showed similar sharing but the comparison was nonrandomized.
A descriptive sample strongly preferred human service agents, demonstrating that machine interaction can also face a trust barrier.

confidence_rationale: One strong framing experiment provides convergent mechanism evidence, qualified by indirect and low-confidence acceptability studies.
